# GEO report: trailhead

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 46–54/100, Unconfirmed → At risk on the low number

Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54.

All results are read from code. The score is low for three reasons:
- The site renders only in the browser, so crawlers get an empty page.
- `/guides` is told not to be indexed.
- Nothing links to `/guides` as a normal link.

The only unknown is the canonical URL, because no site domain is declared. No score cap applied, because the home page is indexable.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Render pages on the server (or prerender them)
- **Why it matters:** with `ssr: false`, crawlers that don't run JavaScript get an empty page, not your headings and text.
- **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2`
- **What the code says:** `ssr: false,`
- **Size:** Medium. Set `ssr: true`, or prerender `/` and `/guides`. If your host already prerenders, a live check would confirm that.
- **Score after this:** 59–67/100

### 2. Stop sending `noindex` for `/guides`
- **Why it matters:** this header asks search engines to leave your main content page out of results, yet the sitemap lists that same page.
- **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:2-3`
- **What the code says:** `if (getRequestURL(event).pathname.startsWith('/guides')) { setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');`
- **Size:** Small. Delete the condition, or restrict it to `/admin`.
- **Score after this:** 52–61/100

### 3. Make the `Sitemap:` line an absolute URL
- **Why it matters:** crawlers expect a full address in robots.txt, and a relative path may be ignored, so they may not find your sitemap.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4`
- **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml`
- **Size:** Small. Use `https://<your-domain>/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 54–63/100

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, plain text with valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks only `/admin` (assumed you want to be found) |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`: `/guides` is noindex, `/` is fine (1 of 2 routes clear). `/admin` is deliberately noindex and not in the sitemap, so it isn't counted. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical per page | Can't tell | No canonical anywhere, and no site domain is declared. The sitemap uses `trailhead.example`, which looks like a placeholder. |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | `nuxt.config.ts:2` has `ssr: false`, and no prerender setting was found |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD structured data is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4` is relative. The sitemap file itself is valid. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | `lang` is set (`nuxt.config.ts:5`). The title `Trailhead` (`app.vue:2`) and description (`nuxt.config.ts:6`) are the same on every route (0 of 2 routes clear). |
| GEO-016 | Key pages reached by real links | Problem | `pages/index.vue:8` (`/guides` 0 of 1 clear) |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't block AI search | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` found in head tags or in the header middleware |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Read `pages/index.vue`, `guides.vue` and `admin.vue`: no images, and the button has text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not an app |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | None present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | None present |

## Other problems found

- **Sitemap lists a noindex page:** `public/sitemap.xml:4` has `<loc>https://trailhead.example/guides</loc>`, while `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` sets `noindex` on it. Fix this together with item 2.
- **Placeholder domain in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3` has `https://trailhead.example/`. Replace `trailhead.example` with your real domain.

## Worth considering

- **Make the `/guides` promise real:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `Routes graded from easy to strenuous.` The page lists no routes. Add the routes with their grade, distance and time, ideally each on its own page such as `/guides/<slug>`.
- **Replace the button with a link:** `pages/index.vue:8`: `<button @click="router.push('/guides')">`. Using `<NuxtLink to="/guides">` fixes GEO-016.
- **Give each page its own title and description:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' })`. Add `useHead` or `useSeoMeta` in each page, for example "Trail guides – Peak District walks | Trailhead".
- **Add substance to the home page:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `Walks across the Peak District`. The page has only a heading and a button. Add a short intro, featured walks and where the area is.
- **Add canonicals once the domain is known:** no canonical is set anywhere. Set `site.url` or `useHead({ link: [{ rel: 'canonical', href }] })` on each page.
- **Add site identity as structured data:** the heading and `Trailhead` title are not machine-readable. `WebSite` and `Organization` JSON-LD (the site name and URL) might help.
- **Add `<lastmod>` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-4` has no dates. Add them if you have real update dates.
- **Generate the sitemap instead of keeping it by hand:** `public/sitemap.xml` is hand-written. A Nuxt sitemap module would keep it in step with your routes.

## Can't tell from code

- **GEO-015 (canonicals):** the intended domain isn't declared. Tell me the real domain and I can settle it.
- **GEO-003 (prerendering):** a host or CDN might prerender the pages outside this repo. A live scan would show what crawlers actually receive.
- **Headers set outside the repo:** none were visible, but the CDN or host config isn't in the repository.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI tools to find this site, apart from `/admin`.
- I read all 9 tracked files: `app.vue`, `nuxt.config.ts`, the three pages, `public/robots.txt`, `public/sitemap.xml`, `server/middleware/headers.ts` and `package.json`. There is no `geo.config.json`. I searched for JSON-LD, canonicals and a prerender configuration and found none.
- I scored `/`, `/guides` and `/admin`, the only routes. `/admin` is excluded from the indexability count because it is deliberately noindex.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
